## Natural history notes

A small leaf beetle characterized by its yellow to tan wing covers marked with bold black stripes or broken dark lines, along with a darker head and thorax. In Florida, it is found around cottonwoods, willows, and related trees in wetlands, river edges, ponds, ditches, parks, yards, and other areas where host trees grow. Both adults and larvae feed on leaves, sometimes skeletonizing foliage when abundant, and they serve as part of the broader food web for birds, spiders, predatory insects, and parasitoid wasps.
